claims.explanation: Vincristine kills cells by binding tubulin and arresting mitosis, and the key determinant of selective sensitivity is whether the resulting mitotic arrest efficiently triggers apoptosis. High expression of the anti-apoptotic BCL2 family member MCL1, or loss of its degradation machinery (FBW7), blunts this death signal and protects cells, whereas low MCL1 and intact FBW7 sensitize. Drug efflux pumps such as ABCB1/MRP1 and altered tubulin (TUBB/TUBA4A) expression or mutations further modulate intracellular drug levels and target engagement.

features.basis: MCL1 is the crucial regulator of apoptosis during antitubulin-induced mitotic arrest; high levels protect
FBW7 loss prevents MCL1 degradation, blunting vincristine-induced apoptosis
P-glycoprotein efflux reduces intracellular vincristine and confers resistance
MRP overexpression confers moderate resistance to vincristine
Tubulin mutations alter the drug-binding site and reduce vincristine target engagement
Alpha-tubulin mutations can destabilize drug binding and reduce sensitivity
Anti-apoptotic BCL2 family signaling opposes mitotic-arrest-induced death
SARM1 NADase activity drives vincristine-induced axonal degeneration, a toxicity rather than tumor-killing mechanism
Loss of p53-mediated apoptosis can reduce cell death after mitotic arrest
Survivin overexpression inhibits apoptosis downstream of mitotic arrest
Virtual cell shows CDK1 downregulation with vincristine; high CDK1 activity is required for mitotic arrest and death
Proliferation-associated gene downregulated in virtual cell response, marking sensitive cycling cells
